changes: Offered as what may clarify even more.
learned: It allows names to be made for lenses while their identity is a shape, not a name: they do not care about the exact content of those names. And at the same time the structure allows to care for those contents - when characters, alphabets, hieroglyphs are captured from the outside world and made sense of through the same system.
over: A sign, a character
saw: A sign, or a character, is itself a lens: it captures predefined shapes as data - a vector, say, for a character - and it allows other lenses to have names, which are arbitrary signs. And again the lenses themselves do not care about those: they do not rely on what data is in a character's lens, only on its relations.

changes: Different from prose: words as relations, and how these relations shape what passes through them - they have information only in their relations. Like now: a lens that gets the current clock; saying now does not say what now is, but it is a shape that lets the time pass through and be projected among other shapes. And we still use a lens to see for ourselves and let the ecosystem reflect it - not leave the vision as foreseeing outside the ecosystem, in our heads or on paper, as dead weight.
learned: That name is itself defined as a lens, when lenses rotate in the data like any other data: a lens is what defines relations in data. So we need a lens that shapes data in such a way that we get a lens as the outcome - a lens that makes lenses - just as there is a lens that heals all other lenses. What is now lenses merges with what is now words: the names of lenses and their relations become words, which is itself a lens that has the shape of all lenses. Another lens named all words that uses the same lens would not matter, as they point to the same; a healing lens would show exactly that. A chain of lenses can be made into another lens and given a name; words chain just like lenses.
over: Lenses and data, of the same nature
saw: We come closer to a point where lenses and data themselves become a hurdle - where we can look at their nature and see that they are of the same nature. A lens is both a viewer of some source, defining a shape in which to continuously place light, and itself a cut and a name for it; and the shape can leave the lens and project onto another surface, and a projection can feed into other lenses. A lens is a name that defines shapes which let light through and project shapes onto surfaces.

changes: We are getting closer and closer to a complete tool that naturally shows them, discovers them as intelligible data from intelligible data. And refining, clarifying, is our first priority when we see such an opportunity - especially when we see it by using OCO and ocoeco - where the act itself can now be reflected with ocoeco.
learned: A milestone is just a praise of a great work that has been done, after it is done - when it was not realized, intelligible and reflected so before it began - or a praise of a great work ahead that fills a gap like the one we discovered, or merges overlaps, or clarifies the whole. So far we have been placing them from outside the ecosystem, just from our heads, out of taste.
over: What a milestone is
saw: It shows the gap, it shows the need, and we have ocoeco to reflect them: naturally we will see from Rhizoid's own data that this can be the next gap to fill, and how best to fill it.

changes: Put poorly, perhaps - just a glimpse to consider. It may shed light on why the language's things have ids and still cannot be pointed at.
learned: A glimpse, a connection of natures: maybe we have arrived naturally at what Rhizome stated at the beginning - graphs, names as aliases, and an intelligible structure that keeps track of the names and the graph's nodes, with an interface to all that. And SQL, and ids, start to bring more friction into the flow itself.
over: Overlapping names, and where this has arrived
saw: What naturally arises as overlaps of ids and names shows us again that these are of the same nature: that a name is not really the place it names; that there can be many names for the same place - and the structure is still intelligible, because exact places do not depend on names. And we have discovered a self-healing process, a lens for lenses, that keeps track of it all and helps prevent unintelligible growth.

changes: Thinking aloud, for consideration.
learned: A need in general always seems to be a need for clarity.
over: What a connection says in prose
saw: The part that enters as prose can be entered as intelligible data: as relations between a need, a decision that is made to fill another need, a need that fills a gap, a need that clarifies an overlap - like the lens that said the same thing two ways.

changes: Running continuously it can be more and more aware of its situation: where now it takes data from its surroundings only when launched, it can treat the surroundings as part of the continuous flow. Me using the window is itself a flow of data; what I am working on becomes intelligible and exactly derivable from what I do in the window; and in progress is not a one-time render but a continuous reflection of observed signals.
learned: When no interaction is done it flows easily, without any noticeable load, like an open window: it shows us what is, what we have so far, its relations. But we can put a finger into that flow - make a connection between something, give it a new name, its relations, how they flow: what lenses currently do that is left behind the brackets of an interface, in Rust code.
over: What ocoeco is
saw: Our ocoeco program is a process of a whole, and like any process it has no defined start and no end. Currently it is treated like a command line: we type something, it starts, takes that in, gives something out and it dies - when the whole thing we have built we see as continuous, and what is changing is the interaction with it.

changes: This itself can be entered as a lens. Two formulations for the same nature are unnecessary in ocoeco, but can be allowed, just highlighted as a projection from the healing lens - to reflect how the world uses words. And correcting by hand a thing we decided should not be set by hand is itself a sign that there may be a gap: to clear overlaps and fill gaps we do not need more handwork, we need clearer seeing. We go insight after insight, by quality, and quantity goes hand in hand none the less - sometimes one sees clearer, sometimes another.
learned: A blank space that shows what can go there, applied to lenses: the whole available area treated not like a terminal, where one can only fill what is left to the right of the line, but as a clickable sheet - where one clicks, he is shown what lens projection can go there. When one is done making that sheet it can itself be made into a word, linux-projects-board: a lens of lenses, that gathers any number of other lenses next to each other and projects them onto a surface. The beauty of it is the same: that lens does not care about the data that will pass those shapes - where to get it, how to shape it, how to project it is all done by those lenses; it only shapes which shapes to place together, and in what shape to project them.
over: Words that cut, a lens of lenses, and a sheet
saw: That the word stops telling things apart is a good sign, because they actually never were apart - this fact just was not in focus before. Words shape information: they focus on one thing and leave another aside; they do the cutting of a whole, but not by themselves - a cut is an arbitrary line that makes sense at the moment, to bring something into focus and leave the rest out as noise, and to project what was looked at onto something else, or let it pass through more lenses, or place projections side by side and get a shape of shapes - intelligible before the screen.

changes: A star is a source only in the sense that its light has already made that trip many times.
learned: This is how healthy language comes together, naturally discovered, as intelligible, reasonable relations: needed is not one thing - known only from what exists. Every word itself becomes intelligible data and conveys relations, reasons - and what they shapeshift into, and because of what.
over: What argenv is, and what words become
saw: Am I seeing something intelligible, clear, concluding that argenv is basically just another lens? It just has a notion of Linux terminals as a surface to project onto, Rust code as a source to get the data for the projection from, and a focus that shapes the projection of the data.

changes: We are moving towards Rhizome - naturally, not as an imposed goal. If our goal were to interact with a crufted world, its isolated programs and its protocols imposed like a law, we could go on making workarounds; but everything we did so far leads to leaving old ways behind and discovering clear, elegant ways - itself not imposed like a rule, but discovered. And it comes outside of being about a program: other spheres that seemed established, isolated, imposed start to click into place - the opposite sign to a friction sign. The word issue - a problem, a failure, being wrong - now hurts our ears.
learned: What argenv does in nature - transparency, self-speaking interactability - cannot really be done without friction and cruft when we split a program into multiple programs and files: we come to the friction sign that Rhizome raises. Its nature can be discovered in what we already have in ocoeco and others, currently split, artificially imposed as separate files and programs. When we look at the whole we see that the cuts are artificially imposed and can move around, can change, and are not to be fixed in a rigid structure like a file, a program, a package. That is why argenv was to be a rhizoid: so that a program could use it as an extension of itself, and not as a black box with a set of rules of how to use it.
over: A rule, a cut, and where this is moving
saw: Here we can see a little friction: a rule would be needed - a rule as something imposed from outside without being derived, discovered from inside. When we derive from inside, discover how something is in a whole, we are able to see gaps and overlaps, to deconstruct, see the nature, merge and dissolve. And more and more exclusions arise while we accept friction and refuse to communicate with a whole.

changes: So that the interaction is not a hassle or a bureaucracy of filling forms.
learned: In progress should be in progress like a reflection of what we do right now - not because we remember to update the state, but because our own work goes through ocoeco, so it can be automatically derived: what we are working on, why and how, the need, the blockages. Everything is tied together already.
over: In progress and waiting, drifting
saw: It had drifted: items in progress whose next steps were already done or blocked. This shows another gap and overlap, just like with milestones: in progress and waiting drift when they are imposed externally and not derived from the data relations that we already have, not derived from the act that we do.

changes: This moves toward the interaction with ocoeco: a glimpse being more like programming with normal words, the interface closer to a shape editor - each relation selected, not entered; selection done by typing, each stroke choosing what fits the next blank spot; just being on a blank spot shows the groups of what can be entered; and the whole entering is itself a shape of shapes, not an unstructured pot of text. If today's terminals bring too much friction, we consume the terminal concept and make one that completes the whole with less - not a decision to make in advance, a process of discovery.
learned: A whole is not changing; a whole is always a whole; we discover it, and a gap is what we do not yet see in it. Being wrong is not wrong: it is a communication process with a whole - when we see it, we answer it, and the friction resolves. Wrongness is only when we stay in a state of friction and ignore the communication with the whole.
over: Healthy language, being wrong, and what entering could become
saw: It does not really never end - not in a bad way, like piling up cruft of redefining words. We discover words by nature: the nature of processes, their states and relations. That process is really infinite, but that is what progress really means: not to accumulate more words but to see the whole clearer and clearer - we do not just add words, we merge, we discover overlaps of the same nature, we simplify, we clarify, and it happens naturally; it becomes visible, evident.

changes: It becomes more evident with the right lens - the natures of words coming together as one ecosystem too.
learned: The gap - the tool not being where one is when one starts thinking; the one who works on the ecosystem most standing outside it - can be traversed, since we have a tool, the ecosystem, for it. It does not just may be: we see clearly that it comes naturally into focus. The need becomes more evident when we have an ecosystem that reflects a whole - a need to elegantly find a stream in it, a place in it, exactly where it has least friction and fits most naturally.
over: ocoeco looking at itself, and the one who stands outside
saw: Another connection that naturally comes into view: ocoeco looking at itself with its ecosystem - it can clarify itself, see what overlaps, what lenses manipulate the same nature and how it can be merged. Is it not the self-healing I was noticing some time ago: healing, as contrary to unintelligible growths of lenses that otherwise themselves would become cruft, and grow like a cancer?

changes: We ourselves come closer and closer to the nature of the whole; all of it naturally starts merging together, like a chain reaction.
learned: If the nature of an entry is taken further, it is a source - like what we have called stars are light sources - but a source that has made round trips from some surfaces.
over: The flow of lenses, and what an entry is
saw: Our lens flow looks more and more like a dataflow with a closed cycle, like an ecosystem; it shapes more like a stream of shapes: a beam of light passing through a lens, reshaping, projecting to a surface, bouncing off a surface - a surface becoming a source of the next light that enters a lens - and the process repeats, each time reshaping, refocusing the light, expanding on the nature of the surfaces to which it projects and from which the next beam can bounce back.

changes: I halted trying the form in the fulldome until we have a self-speaking, touchable, transparent system thanks to argenv, and not another program that dictates how to use it somewhere behind brackets: I do not want the experience to be the same shape as what we are trying to clarify and simplify with everything we do.
learned: We naturally come to see for ourselves - in the shapes of our data, in relations, in our experience - that problems are not a thing to solve, to countermeasure: they are just indicators that something does not clearly fit the whole; something is stale, overlapping, something is lacking.
over: The words problem and countermeasure, and what they lead to
saw: That language leads to cruft and excuses in anything it touches - especially in software: versions hell, exceptions, exclusions, tests that are dead weight. We now have the ecosystem mindset, and implement and perfect it as OCO and ocoeco.

changes: For looking from somewhere else we have the solution at our fingertips: making somewhere else into somewhere here. Is that not what our lenses are doing - they bring something that is remote into focus, weave a new surface of data into existing data, shape it, simplify where the overlap naturally arises, and project it back onto a new surface, or the same surface in a shifted shape. A note, so as not to miss a sign when that moment comes - the ecosystem mindset implemented in the toolset, not kept away in someone's head.
learned: We have a way to see that perfects itself, that naturally shows where artificial cuts restrict us: where we can move the whole as one, still having cuts, but with a way to make a cut in any place and still get the whole - because it is whole before we cut it, and cuts are just shapes, shapes of shapes, that can change shape without losing data. That is what natural movement in the ecosystem is.
over: A constellation, an observatory, what is the lab's - and looking from somewhere else
saw: These are not fixed rules: they are just current excuses, formalities, and they do not have to stay that way - seeing the whole becomes clearer and simpler when they are not. They too are excuses even though I made them; they are no better than any other excuse in the world: they were made to interact with the rigid, fixed surfaces defined by the old world. What the lab does is the lab's is itself an imposed line, cut from outside - a small sign already, which will become more evident when we try to interact with a phone from ocoeco.

changes: The first step holds. What it left behind: one program that did the work and was also the only way to hear of it.
learned: lab-agent was a necessity of the purpose, not of architecture: hands, for a driver who had none. Reasoned: within two days it held three jobs in one program - running the work, speaking to the author, showing a board - each asked for by a real need to witness; that joining is what later let one failure silence everything.
over: How we came here, 1: why there is a lab at all (April to 9 November)
saw: Read, in an earlier conversation of 1 April: the Observatory was first written down as what watches and does not build - only its own instruments. Recorded: the canon was seeded on 21 September, text as data cut from a working repository. Read, in the sessions of October: snapall taught the working ways - every layer is the top of the layers beneath it, measure before claiming, guards over memory - gathered into the playbook by 5 November. Read: on 8 November the phone's work began on real hardware and lab-agent was born that day, pulling jobs over git, because the one driving could not touch the phone.

changes: The principle was right on the first day. The distance between a decision and the machine that carries it is what the next three days were spent closing.
learned: The observatory was a necessity of the whole: what cannot be seen is steered by memory. Reasoned: but it was founded inside the ecosystem's own organization and drawn by one engine whose views were written by hand - so views are data was true in words and not in the machine. And April's rule, that the observatory watches and does not build, was crossed unnoticed: the place that looked and the thing that was built shared one home.
over: How we came here, 2: 10 November, an observatory in one day
saw: Read: by 10 November the phone alone was a kernel, docs, lab tools, device profiles and a catalogue of 46 capabilities, and beside it stood Rhizome, Rhizoid, Mnemonic Vocabulary, argenv and tad; the grand picture was asked for. Recorded: that day the observatory was founded - the mark, discovery, the harvest, an engine in Rust - with decisions that already said what took three more days to make true: a project tells its idea, path, workings and work in its own data; nothing may depend on anyone remembering; an observatory of a commons cannot be the only one allowed to look - views are data, with no privileged path.

changes: This is the last day the purpose and the instrument moved forward together. That night the instrument failed.
learned: Each was necessary for the one before: a picture needs data; data needs a language; a language needs an engine that can be trusted and delivered. Recorded: two practices were broken on the day they were written, both resting on memory alone - which is why every practice was made to name the check that carries it.
over: How we came here, 3: 11 November, the picture must follow the work
saw: Recorded: The whole first - the author: do not bury yourself in one thing; perfect connected processes. And the same day, Back to the purpose: more of the phone, measured - its checks widened to 27, the microphone's chain nearly whole. For the picture to follow, work had to record itself: glimpses, land's guards, the shared language declared as data, and tad rewritten in Rust so that Python left its backbone.

changes: oco-agent: a journal for every job, run once by construction, a lease for each driver, a core that speaks its own words - born beside lab-agent and trusted with nothing until it had watched it.
learned: The root named that night - a job is a script with no record of its life - was true, and under it lay a plainer one found only by looking: a listing believed whole that was not. Reasoned: the incident did not come from the architecture work. It came from growth without it - three jobs in one program, and done inferred from an absence.
over: How we came here, 4: the night of 11 November
saw: Recorded, measured: lab-agent stopped starting jobs at 22:29 and after a reboot replayed 102 finished ones; no alert could reach the author - every channel went through the agent. Harm: none. The cause, proven the next day: a directory listing that stops at 1,000 entries and does not say so. Read: the author - no one to blame; redesign the whole thing with the full picture in mind; a heartbeat, so that work stops when the one who asked is gone.

changes: What was written down as the last condition of a switch is the oldest need on the route - a person's own hands - and it is still open.
learned: For safety, yes. For the switch, not yet. Recorded: lab-agent's daemon still runs, because two things it did had not been made again - the board on the author's phone, and a way for the author himself to drive. Reasoned: the first is since done in another shape (what is new in view). The second is the one thing lab-agent gave that was taken away and not given back: on 10 November the author could answer in a box on a board; today the fulldome can only be read.
over: How we came here, 5: was the redesign's need met?
saw: Recorded: oco-agent refused exactly the 102 replays when that night's log was run through its rules, parked its work when killed, and on 12 November ran every job the AI driver asked - 110, none through lab-agent. Its pulse is received outside the lab, and it speaks.

changes: Reasoned: it is also where the purpose stopped being worked on. The phone's last session is 11 November: the microphone's route is set, the stream does not start.
learned: Reasoned: here the route turned from repairing to refining, and it was a necessity of another kind - not that something had broken, but that the next thing asked for, a board any place could have, could not be made honestly on views written by hand for one observatory. The decision of 10 November had to become true. Relations declared, the language held by lenses, a focus as data, the problems lens: each was the smallest thing the one before could stand on.
over: How we came here, 6: why mending a board became designing the whole
saw: Recorded: oco-agent needed a board, and one over every backlog was built in an hour. The author: a board is the room, not a list; then, not a room but a sky; then, not one observatory but many. Looking at what the picture kept found 860 links held by discipline alone, and the largest gap of all: nothing showed problems - 21 release runs had failed unseen.

changes: What is true between the stars had no home until 13 November. Practices are the clearest case: rules for every star, kept in one observatory's own data.
learned: The instrument earned its keep by what it showed that no one was looking for. Recorded: and a lesson does not travel between stars - it was learned three times, in three places. Reasoned: the rounds on projection, shape and screen turned inward; the author said so - important when they improve the vision, not as a game of looks - and they were rightly stopped there. What they left is real (a shape checked with no data) but it was not what the whole lacked.
over: How we came here, 7: what the refining found, and where it wandered
saw: Recorded: on its first day the problems lens was asked what had failed on main unheard - 111 runs in three days, three of them real and unheard for days. A token said to be gone sat in ten repositories. And the lesson written as practice 25 on 12 November had been written before: on 3 November in the playbook - a guess written as fact, corrected - and on 10 November in the observatory - two practices broken the day they were written.

changes: So the order: first the person's hands - an entry and an answer made from the fulldome. Then the practices to OCO's place, so a lesson is learned once. Then the engine's views against the fulldome, and parent with them. And then the purpose: the measure of all of it is whether the microphone's stream is easier to start than it was on 11 November.
learned: Reasoned: the three are one question asked three times - where a thing lives, and who can reach it from where. The first observatory held three things in one place: one person's looking (now his own observatory); what is true for every star - the practices, how we work - which belongs in OCO's place by the reasoning that moved seven decisions there; and the engine's hand-written views, which end when the fulldome shows as much. Retiring it restores April's rule. parent is the flat roof of 10 November - one parent for nineteen of twenty-two; what it meant is said by what a place gathers, and it goes with the views that read it. And the author's driving is not the last step of a switch but the first need of the route come round again: lab-agent began as hands for a driver who had none, and the one without hands now is the person whose work it is.
over: How we came here, 8: what the route says of the three things left
saw: Three things do not yet click: two observatories publish; parent in every mark says what is no longer true; the author cannot yet drive from the fulldome. And using the system to look back showed four more: necessity has no link (a decision can refine a decision, and work can serve one, but nothing says this exists because of that problem); looking back shows only the newest; one cannot look through a constellation from an observatory; and lab-agent, where most of this happened, has one session recorded.

changes: Probing blindly, hoping it can be seen how it is already done in the world - btrfs, Clojure, databases that are not really tables - and how it suits us better. Will it be fitting to do such research? Maybe we can find glimpses of how what we are dealing with was dealt with in the world.
learned: Tables are themselves just a particular shape of data: exactly like a lens, they do not care about what is in them so long as it does not contradict their shapes. Do we really need a middle man in the form of a table? Our system gets closer to being able itself to define such a middle man - a lens that works with tables and gives tables as a shape - but even seeing that, I do not see why we would want to pass all our lenses through such a table lens.
over: Tables, and a graph
saw: Can you look at how tables serve us at the moment? Do they really do something that a graph of the best kind cannot? Thinking about squares on the periphery of what we are making feels off. It feels like a tree - upright, and downright seen as roots - but it makes no difference, as what branches end at is a surface; where upper branches meet lower ones in some nodes, going in one direction, the direction of a lens; and lenses themselves look like branches.

changes: As I claimed from the beginning: everything should be transparent - an elegant ecosystem as a core, as its nature, that makes this possible, and the process of making it itself transparent, self-speaking, interactive.
learned: tad was made as an excuse to interact with what the world has, GitHub and git; and other excuses travelled into our design - HTML and CSS because that is what GitHub Pages offers, a terminal view because that is what Linux terminals offer. If our ecosystem benefits from native graphs, I would rather drop the excuse of complying, at least as a research prototype on the lab. And a lens of lenses that shows the relations of lenses, not the shapes they project: a line where information enters a lens, its name, how its focus cuts off parts of the data, a line that ends shortly showing what was cut off, and a line that continues into other lenses or down to a surface - and, a click away, a fulldome projection shrinking into a line, a beam, to see how it got there.
over: Graphs, the excuses we comply with, and the beam
saw: The most elegant systems the world made so far are graphs: git is a graph, btrfs on the lab is a graph, respected databases that present tables are graphs; Clojure, treating data as graphs, treated itself as data and became a graph - the same move we have been striving towards: define an ecosystem and move its definition into itself, so that the definition becomes the ecosystem, and its value is in interacting with it - able, through intuitive, self-explanatory interaction, to refine itself, grow and shrink, fill gaps and merge overlaps, take from sources and project onto them.

changes: Just like the natural rotation of things in an ecosystem. Just to consider.
learned: Where in Rhizome the very use of memory would become an accumulating dead weight, ocoeco has a lens of lenses, with which it can be intelligible that branches which do not lead to any interface - source, lens, source - automatically dissolve into free memory.
over: What Rhizome stated, what ocoeco arrived at, and what lets go
saw: What Rhizome stated, ocoeco arrived at naturally, as an ecosystem - and with such a set of lenses as allow us to see gaps and overlaps in Rhizome itself. Where Rhizome just concluded that the graph will grow indefinitely, and physical storage is finite, ocoeco has already seen it before and found a cure for itself.

changes: Does it bring order into how lenses stack and go side by side; is the whole structure simpler and cleaner reviewed with all the images we have made - and can the review itself be reflected with ocoeco, thanks to lenses and the self-speaking design.
learned: Lenses side by side, with their projections, are themselves a shape of shapes: a plane-lens - with instances such as a fulldome of some stars, filled with other lenses. Lenses stacked one after another: the preceding projection plane becomes what the next lens reads from, making it a filter, because a lens by its nature can only read what is and leave out what its focus does not pass. Inside the ecosystem lenses use planes as input and output; toward the outside world another part of a lens captures a place's real-world data and its shape, and outputs to some real-world surface - a 2d plane, a screen of squares with its own ways of moving them (wrapping, new lines), unlike a canvas of squares.
over: Awareness of a plane
saw: What we call a projection, which can be a projection of projections, is a projection plane - all shapes of shapes in one plane - an intelligible plane much easier to feed into another plane of lenses, a lens of lenses where shapes are placed side by side, before it hits a surface and results in a mess of whatever shapes that surface can hold, losing the data's shape; reading it again into intelligible shapes is more work than using the plane that exists just before shapes and data hit a surface.

changes: It brings clarity to the next step: the view to open and move in needs no design of its own - it is the lenses, in focus, on one more surface.
learned: It is a lens that renders the same shining of stars, through a lens, into focus, laid out into a terminal view.
over: What lab-agent's board is, now
saw: What was a lab-agent board before is now just lenses focusing - like a lens that focuses into .md structures, or html and css structures.

changes: It fits the full picture: lenses made of lenses, down from the fulldome.
learned: A colour lens: a lens that uses other lenses to make what they already focus more beautiful or convenient - like making the infographics our previous webpage had.
over: Lenses over lenses
saw: We will be able to add more lenses, where again naming is discovered naturally.

changes: The render agreement becomes part of ocoeco's language and mark. The order stands: the fulldome researched lens by lens; one lens made real on one star, as something to open and touch; a constellation's lens; an observer gathering renders.
learned: A dome is one sky, so the word wall is not replaced - it disappears, and a part of the whole is simply a lens: one word fewer, and what is connected is seen as connected. Fulldome carries what no board did: the story a star tells, time, intent. It also parts two things I had blurred: the observatory observes what is real; the fulldome shows it to people - the author's user-facing part is the fulldome. One caution keeps the word honest: a planetarium's audience only watches, and ours must touch and act. And an agreement kept in a tool is followed by using the tool; one kept on paper is followed by remembering - which is the difference ocoeco exists to make.
over: The author's two corrections: fulldome for room, and ocoeco as the agreement itself
saw: Room and wall came from a factory and brought its shape: walls divide - purpose here, work there. I had also set the agreement on renders beside ocoeco, as a protocol to be written and followed.

changes: A watcher must itself be watched. Listings are read whole or not at all. Every new mechanism's proof names the event that proves it. Lessons go into reflections, so the next session inherits them. And a caution for the vision: 'click into place' is proven only when a project outside this circle adopts ocoeco on its own; until then the format must stay small, documented and robust, and that matters more than the user-facing part.
learned: Prove each mechanism by its own evidence, not by the path around it: I proved the watcher's alert, never its schedule. Prefer what says when it is cut short or stuck over what fails quietly. Look before editing: four failed edits came from guessing at code I had not read. The author's questions moved the design more than my plans did - each driver its own lease, the name oco-agent, tad's one concern, the shared GitHub budget. And on the author's larger point: open source has intelligence from the outside - CHAOSS has measured activity since 2017 - but not the inside: why things are so, what was decided and rejected, what is needed next and who is doing it. That inside is what ocoeco records, oco-agent coordinates and the observatory presents - the analysis half of BI and BA, which nobody had put in place.
over: 2026-11-11 evening to 2026-11-12 morning: tad's lost reasons restored and connected, SQL back in tad, oco-agent from its core to a service, the replays, and the watcher that never watched
saw: Every serious failure was silent. A listing that stopped at 1,000 without saying so made lab-agent run finished work again, twice. A request with no time limit most likely froze it. A schedule that never fired left the watcher blind for a night. A client stripped lines from inside a script. The shadow could not see jobs older than itself. And tad's reason to exist sat in a session log and an unmerged spike, so a rewrite dropped its SQL. Each time, what saved the work was a record that could be read cold, or a check that refused instead of passing.

changes: I am not declaring what is best: I bring views and thoughts into consideration, so that the whole becomes clearer and more complete, hand in hand.
learned: The wordings a room and a wall do not really fit the whole. I think fulldome does - like a planetarium dome. ocoeco, as that agreement and that convenient way which allows all of this, is the next, wider view of what all those efforts of the world were striving to achieve with what they call a board. A planetarium dome does not just show constellations, as our constellations' lenses do: it shows a story behind them - relations, a history, intent.
over: The room, its walls, and the agreement on what a render is
saw: The agreement on what a render is - that is what ocoeco is for: it is the agreement and a convenient way to follow it automatically, not principles on paper somewhere, nor a ritual, nor a discipline in someone's head.

changes: I bring views for consideration; the plan stands.
learned: Currently OCO as a project is a bit mixed up with my projects. OCO as a project is a part of the ecosystem that allows me to have my observatory, where all my projects come together - each constellation having its own fulldome, and all of them can be brought together under observatories.
over: The fulldome, and what OCO is
saw: The point of OCO is that it is not one observatory. Anyone will be able to create their observatories, and they - all or some - can be brought together, to share their views on the sky.

changes: Before building more, the room is researched wall by wall. Then a lens is made real on one star, then a constellation's lens, then an observer gathering renders. I keep asking, before adding anything: which wall of the room is this, and does it make the whole simpler.
learned: The room and the author's four words are one design: a wall is a lens, the room is what an observer shows of a constellation, so the board needs no entity of its own. Three things planned apart - the renderer leaving tad, presentation as data, the observatory engine's hand-written views - are one: lenses declared as data. Open commons add what Toyota's room never needed: nobody is assigned, so the room must invite. Two things must be faced for the design to hold: a view across stars needs their data, not their renders, so it belongs to the constellation and is rendered there; and gathering renders needs a small agreement on what a render is. The word lens already named a kind of project here; that becomes constellation, and a star may then belong to several.
over: The board built on 2026-11-12, set against what the author meant by it
saw: I had taken one wall for the room: a flow of backlog items, because the backlog was the first thing we had. The obeya began because no one person held the knowledge the Prius needed; its walls showed purpose, plan, progress, problems and countermeasures together so that problems became visible. ocoeco's entities already are those walls - nothing had to be invented, only seen.

changes: OCO and ocoeco will naturally expand into being a part of software: a user-facing part, robust and at one's fingertips, not depending on a web browser - a way for users to be connected to what they use: to see their apps' progress and the progress of the Linux phone they use, to see what needs focus and add their part, fill in the necessary pieces of information, make the necessary tests, provide feedback.
learned: ocoeco is the basic unit - a format, a protocol, a way of interacting with it, and of its interconnection: an ecosystem, for real.
over: Years of watching open source; the months since a research with Claude; what OCO and ocoeco have become
saw: Any big tech, any business has BI. Open source is not a business, and no one clicked into place that it lacks BI and BA - coordination, analysis, presentation. Now there is a working soul for it, OCO and ocoeco, which makes it possible with a simple and portable system, where ocoecos click into place with one another.

changes: I was not sure whether the fulldome is just a name for one lens, nor did I see the observer's place clearly: perhaps the part of ocoeco that allows the gathering of gatherings, where an observatory is tied to a physical location. We both should carefully consider the full picture.
learned: The fulldome is what today's world calls a board, taken to its full potential, realized in ocoeco's database structure and its lenses. A lens is a concept and a concrete mechanism: how it gathers its data and where it gets it - standing in the middle, at the hot places where things are fresh, as ocoeco stands before git - and how it can be presented: a structure of .md files, HTML and CSS, or any other. When a lens is done, anyone in the ocoeco system can use it in their star or constellation and it will just work - no fiddling with feeding data or how to present it: the data and its structure are known. That anyone can have an observatory blurs the line between a user and a contributor - the line Rhizome is later meant to remove completely.
over: Star, constellation, observatory, fulldome, lens and observer, after the back and forth
saw: Star, constellation and observatory all come from a need for separate places for all of this to actually be somewhere physically; they are git repos currently. A star's part in ocoeco is that it is what produces data. A constellation's part is that it gathers its stars' data into a group, where their fulldomes are parts of one wider fulldome. We could leave only star and observatory, but then the relations between projects have nowhere to live: a constellation is a family of projects - they work independently, but they benefit from each other and have a shared purpose - like the oco repo as a constellation, ocoeco its star, oco-agent another, and other stars OCO may need. An observatory repo does the actual observing of constellations: it can have several, their fulldomes seen separately per constellation or star, and as a whole - the same fulldome backbone from ocoeco, gathered from many.

changes: I do not yet see just the right next natural step, how exactly projections can be a self-aware process. In the world's terms a reliable program need not be aware of its process, and when it is not reliable we made the program wrong - but that feels wrong: self adjusting, and awareness of the output of what is actually done, should be a part of a program.
learned: What we have on different surfaces are results of projections, and while the data is intelligible in the form of a projection we can make a self check of what is being projected before it reaches the surface, not after it. Not even tests: taking to the full potential the awareness, for the thing that does it, of what it does.
over: How what surfaces show can be checked without tests that are dead ends
saw: How can it be done when the resulting surfaces are unstructured pots of text, Markdown, HTML? By taking a step back in the process: we have structured data just before it is put into a surface - a projection.

changes: Set aside, at least for now; maybe it will come naturally into focus later.
learned: It would drift meaning from the actual data into someone's head - of what someone thinks is beautiful, more important - without reflecting in the ecosystem, blurring the meanings of dome and surfaces. What we have already proves beautiful: it allows treating text as a surface to focus data on, with bars that are not hand written, not some separate text-processing library, but a natural outcome of the ecosystem.
over: The colour lens, reconsidered
saw: That is exactly why we consider what we say to each other and do not just dictate orders. In that way I do not see what a colour lens clarifies.

changes: The terminal interface of ocoeco glimpse will have a composed view for all current glimpses from lenses, with their defined ergonomics, that allow not to retype what already is and not to dial in what can be got from the computer.
learned: One lens, one glimpse in it; and the glimpse not only defines a place and relations for data, it also defines how to gather them with a convenience. ocoeco glimpse gathers together all glimpses from all lenses - their subcommands and flags, thanks to argenv: non-colliding, and collisions will be flagged by Rust in the creation process, never in use, by Rust's design.
over: The glimpse, the lens, and how data gets its structure
saw: Our earlier concept of glimpses now has a place to fit in: a glimpse is a part of a lens. So far our database structure has been rigidly dictated by us, from outside of the system; now it naturally fits in: lenses that are defined, define the data structure that they need, with glimpses.

changes: OCO in more detail: an oco-star is one entity - an idea, a project; an oco-constellation is a group of stars viewed together as connected; an oco-lens is a way of presenting - sets of predefined SQL requests and renderings of them, which is one thing, into .md, .txt, HTML and CSS or anything else, over the same underlying data; an oco-observer makes no lenses and renders none of others: it looks at other projects' rendered lenses and the lenses themselves and brings them into its own lens render, as the observatory does today. OCO becomes the home of all observers: it gathers them by their marks and takes their renders, re-rendering nothing.
learned: I am open and eager to learn, but not knowledge as expertise by cramming - a pile of random facts and hindrances one just has to know - instead of making it easy to know by seeing and touching what it does: a terminal interface on a command line rather than a twenty-page manual, even when the manual writes itself. Adding more words is not our concern; reflecting a whole, an ecosystem, is - seeing how processes fit, where their intersections can be made simpler and the whole clearer, instead of growing into the cumbersome complexity many of the world's board concepts became.
over: The research on the board, and how much had come to centre on the backlog
saw: By researching the board I meant that ocoeco needs full awareness of what is called a board: the best of the best from the world's experience in that field, with the corporate money squeeze, the pep talk and the bullshit taken out. What ocoeco is, is the next step for open commons - wider than open source - of what Toyota calls obeya, one room where everyone sees the whole: as a principle, as a system, as an implementation that delivers it. Too much was centred on the backlog, as if it were the only thing needed; it started that way because I only knew a word here and there of what the world's best experience has to offer.

changes: The plan's order stands - declare the relations, the problems lens, the invitation, how a finding is known, lenses as data. To it: the mark says what a place gathers (many to many, replacing a single parent); ocoeco's gathering is named observe; a first lens is built to prove the definition before anything is generalized.
learned: The fulldome is a lens and the whole at once, because a lens may be made of lenses and the fulldome is the outermost. The observer is ocoeco's gathering, one act at every scale, until now named harvest and discover. What earns constellation its word beside observatory is belonging against looking. A constellation also keeps data of its own - what is decided for its stars together had nowhere to live: I had been writing such decisions into whichever star was at hand. And my worry over data or renders dissolves: a shared lens shows the same data the same way anywhere.
over: The author's picture, sorted by kind
saw: We had been mixing three kinds of words - places, ways of seeing, and acts. Sorted, each word has one job, and both of the author's doubts answer themselves from his own sentences.

changes: What was declared these two days - the tables, the relations - is regrouped by lens, not rewritten. The first lens built shows both faces: a glimpse one can open and fill, and a showing one can open and read.
learned: A lens has two faces - in and out - and the way in follows from the declaration, so my caution is not needed. The act I called record already had its word. Lenses do depend on each other, by reading; that is safe because they are additive. Finding collisions at build is the rhizoid way, and it - not a rule - is what keeps lenses from becoming plugins. The word glimpse now names a definition, a thing taken in, and the older table of work done; the last needs settling when it is built.
over: The author's resolution: a glimpse is a part of a lens
saw: The shared language's fourteen tables sat in one file we wrote by hand, outside any lens, and ocoeco note asked one to know tables and fields. I had made a lens's own way of gathering data optional, for fear of a plugin system.

changes: We will wrap it into itself later: bringing an awareness to the programs we made about what they actually do, look and interact like - a test wrapped into the design. Tests, now dead ends, become part of the program functioning, giving it the ability to self heal and bringing meaning to what is actually happening, where today exceptions tell nothing about what the thing really does and how well, and are useless to other programs.
learned: What we called the fulldome is a lens that focuses all lenses onto all their surfaces; and dome is a core term - the concept of a surface that stars' shine can be focused onto, the interface for surfaces of lenses to implement, be it Markdown, HTML and CSS, a terminal or whatever someone will come up with in the future.
over: Words settling, and what tests could become
saw: We naturally start to discover words in the ecosystem - a word settled: surface - meaning it really starts living and breathing as an ecosystem. And the ability to finally see and touch what is made.

changes: The projection looks at itself for what is true of every projection. What a lens expects of its own - that there is at least one star, that a total equals a count - has no shape yet; and a part with no answers cannot yet tell that its line names something wrong.
learned: There are two kinds of wrong. A program that is wrong is mended, and tests at its making are right for that: there the world's view holds. But a world that is not what the program assumed cannot be removed by any correctness. So awareness is not a crutch for an unreliable program: it is how a correct program meets an unreliable world - it knows what its own output must be, and looks each time it runs.
over: The author's knot: need a reliable program be aware of what it does?
saw: Every failure of 2026-11-11 and 12 came from a program that was right by its own tests: a listing that stopped at 1,000 entries, a schedule that did not fire, a guard that had never met its collision, runs that fed back into themselves, a date stored as a date.

changes: At this point it mixes with focus, as focus gives shape to data: the shape that focusing makes is a projection. And it answers what was left open - what a lens expects of its own projection, and the part with no answers.
learned: A projection does not check what it projects; it does not touch the data, it does not read text; it defines and self-checks the shape in which that data is projected. When we look at what a surface's text was just before it became a bunch of text, we see the projection and its shapes - a line, lines that make a paragraph, how it is all laid out next to each other, or a shape like a progress bar where we do not care whether it is 1 of 9 or 7 of 9. Like a shadow on a screen that lets half the light pass through.
over: The word project, and what a projection checks
saw: That project is the word we set aside is not a reason to reject projection: it is a sign we are getting the whole clearer. What a project is, in its essence, really is a projection onto some surface - where the preceding processes, where the light came from (an idea, a notion, a need to satisfy, a real urgency), are left behind brackets in today's world. What we do here is shedding a light onto it all, bringing it all into awareness.

changes: A way to step out of surfaces as resulting file formats, toward real-world surfaces, which they are: in the end it all comes to data appearing on some 2d surface of some screen.
learned: A projection is a shape of shapes that is itself a shape as a whole - like a puzzle: the pieces are shapes with joints, and clicked together they are guaranteed to make another shape, because we first define the big shape (a line is 80 monospaced characters wide, lines sit on top of each other) and carve the other shapes in it. If some text editor does not meet the requirements and the result looks wrong, the projection tells exactly why: it defined the shape, the constraints, the borders, how the shapes are laid out together.
over: Text as a screen, and projections as shapes of shapes
saw: A text pot of continuously wrapped lines that fill any volume is one shape of how text projects, and not the only one. If we constrain the volume - by line width, by how many monospaced characters fit in a line - the text becomes a screen: with monospaced characters we can project data onto text as onto a screen, as with the progress bar but taken to a wider potential.

changes: And a caution for the whole: details and surfaces are important when they improve our vision and fit the whole - not when it is a naming game or a looks game. Not more than seeing the whole and making sure everything clicks together as an ecosystem.
learned: Those pieces are guaranteed to make a whole and their places are fixed, because it was a whole and each piece of it had exactly one place. Projection is just the topmost shape of shapes; projection and what it projects onto come hand in hand, like ports and adapters. In a line, a placeholder will never come before the word that precedes it - not because it cares what the word means: it is guaranteed by how the projection is cut into shapes and how they come back together.
over: Where a projection's guarantee comes from
saw: This guarantee does not come from a set of rules. If we look at how puzzles are made, they start as a whole to begin with: anyone can do a puzzle of his own, without any rules of what the individual shapes must be, just by taking some picture and cutting it into pieces.

changes: One place the code is behind the idea: a line is already a finished string when it reaches a surface - a small pot of text one level down - so a page cannot make a star a link. The measure is the only shape kept whole; lines should be kept as their named values until the surface.
learned: There was no missing form: I was asking one layer to do another's work. The data is sound or not in the data; all of it was gathered or not in observing; only the shape is the projection's - and a shape needs no data. It also sets right what I said of the two kinds of wrong: they belong to layers. A shape is the program's own, checked in the making and not watched after; the world is met in observing, and checked there each time. And project and projection are one word - thrown forward: the clash was the picture confirming itself.
over: The author's correction: a projection checks its shape, not its data
saw: I had asked how a lens should declare that there is at least one star, or that a total equals a count, and said I could not see its form; and I had checked a part's shape against its first answer, so a part with no answers could say nothing. I had also taken the clash with the word project as a reason to keep away from projection.

changes: It is the most complex lens and glimpse so far, and time-taking: one has to read through the data and make the connections. With projections, an agent should be able to use the projection before it hits the final pot as its interface - entering this vast picture through a terminal is effort-consuming even for it.
learned: A story can be made with ocoeco, the way our lenses work: data joined, a summary written about it, an insight for the summary, summaries joined into a story with its overall insight. Not only linked, but connected - that from x followed y, z, d, and from them g - chained visibly on the projection and its surface. One summary is an insight of connections that are just history; another reflects relations that were unseen. Red lines that can go through any data we have, to draw insights from their relations and show it all.
over: What a story loses when it is written, and the other side of knowledge and research
saw: So far we have knowledge as if it had a value in itself, when it points to facts; and research as dead gathering of facts and looking around - without the other side: getting insights, seeing connections where they have not been seen before, seeing where things overlap and where there are gaps, how the whole fits together. The story of how we came here is prose: a pot that lost the relations it had just one step before.

changes: Unsettled, and left so: two shapes are nested - the shape of the data (lines, a measure), the same for every surface, and that shape fitted into a volume. On 2026-11-12 projection was recorded as the first; the author uses it for the second, and optics agrees with him (a projection onto a dome is not the one onto a wall). His phrase may be the answer - a shape of shapes that is itself a shape: the word may cover the nest. To settle by use.
learned: A surface is not a file format but a volume with requirements, and laying out is fitting shapes into it, each with a joint for when the space is tight; without that rule there is no guarantee, only hope. With it the guarantee can be checked on the shape before anything is written.
over: The author's screen, and which shape the word projection names
saw: I had made text as a screen twice without naming it: the terminal surface carves one rectangle into others and was tested at a stated volume (110 by 16, 130 by 32); and the bar of ten cells assumed monospace without saying so - a requirement relied on and never declared.
